correctness.rationale: The frozen graph-associahedron package defines P=Σ_{∅≠A⊆L,∅≠B⊆R}Δ_{A∪B}, M=(2^p−1)(2^q−1), N=p+q, Σx_i=M, with p,q≥2. Standard nestohedron support yields x(T)≥z(T)=(2^a−1)(2^b−1) for non-singleton proper connected tubes (a,b≥1), while singleton support is zero. Summing N singleton-ball inequalities gives r≤M/√[N(N−1)], with equality forcing center (M/N)1. Set F(a,b)=z(T)/[k(k−1)], k=a+b. The exact ratio F(a+1,b)/F(a,b)=(2+1/(2^a−1))(k−1)/(k+1), equal to 1 only at (a,b)=(1,1) and strictly >1 for k≥3; coordinatewise path to p,q≥2 contains a strict step. Therefore z(T)/M<k(k−1)/[N(N−1)], and projected tube normal norm √[k(N−k)/N] gives distance >r for all 2≤k<N. For each singleton distance=r. N+M−1 facet count follows from N singleton tubes and M−1 proper mixed tubes. Independently verified 1,872 rational tube pairs p,q in 2..9; not a substitute for the ratio proof.

value.rationale: The complete bipartite graph-associahedron is a natural, exponentially faceted family. An all p,q formula for its exact intrinsic inball, unique center and full tangency orbit provides a meaningful natural geometric invariant and a structural domination principle; it is not an arbitrary finite table or solely a re-expression of the facet count.
